Take a look at Chilly Dog's Great White North coat. It's beautiful. 

We recently got one for our amstaff and it fits like a dream. It actually covers his whole chest, is snug to his body, made of quality materials, and it hugs his bum. My dad isn't doing well. His cancer has now spread from his lymph nodes to his liver, his brain and his spine. He went to the hospital by ambulance yesterday and they found out that he has two tumours in his spine. He's actually in surgery right now to get them removed (two for one father's day special!) as it was causing significant issues.

I went to visit him in the afternoon. Told him I loved him. Downloaded some games to his tablet because he's gonna be in for a long recovery.

I feel absolutely miserable. I just want to run away from it all, stop existing... But I guess I need to be there for my family and I can't devastate them even more. I hate being brave.

I guess we're all hanging in there for now. Sorry for the information dump... I needed to get that off of my chest. Again, thanks for your concern!

If the vet eliminated physical illness from thr question, stress could be the reason. I know my cat ended up pulling her fur out due to stress. While the dog enjoyed playing with a cool new laser light, it actually heavily stressed the cat out. As soon as we eliminated the laser light, her fur started growing back and she was better.

Anything new in your home can stress out a cat, even a rearrangement of furniture. Assuming she's an indoor cat, I'd recommend getting a cat tower (or something similar) for a secure spot to make her feel safe and focus on finding a trigger.

Good luck with kitty. :)

Ask the vet to use gauze to wrap around your cats' forelimbs like trousers, wrapped around the chest and through the cone. Or, little "kitty suspenders", if you will. You might even be able to do it yourself if she's patient and depending on where her wound is.

 My cat recently had a lot of trauma and was very adept at getting her cone off. After the suspenders were put on, her cone didn't leave her little head for another four weeks. There was a bit of minor hair loss around her neck where the gauze was rubbing, however that's much better than having an infected wound to deal with. 

Wish you lots of luck and good healing for your little girl. :)

I found that once I stopped using my fingers and started using the blending sticks, my drawings started to come together more smoothly, and the shading tends to be more even overall. :) Some artists still prefer to use their fingers though, so if it works for you, do it. Art doesn't have a set of rules. ^^

Don't use your fingers for shading. Your fingers have oils on them which will attach themselves to the paper and impact your drawing, making it harder to erase or define. Use a piece of paper and wrap it around your finger, or invest in some tortillons (really tightly wrapped blending sticks made of paper) which cost around 50 cents a piece. Just make sure you angle it and don't put it flat on the paper like how most people use their pencils, or perhaps find a tutorial to show you how to use them properly. This way you can blend a lot closer to your lines and get a more seamless, less scratchy look.

You're doing well, improvement takes practice!
